text:
Sportsnet's headline quoted Zayne Parekh: "I feel like I belong." At 20, in his first full season, the Flames' ninth overall pick is making the case with the power play. Five of his 7 points have come with the man advantage, and he's averaging 18 minutes a night.

Kevin Bahl's season-ending Achilles injury will push him further. In the first game without Bahl he played 22:20, his season high, and picked up two assists. Calgary is almost six points better in its share of expected goals (the quality of chances) with Parekh on the ice than without.

The comparison that matters: of the 25 defensemen picked 7th to 11th since 2005 with four-plus seasons, the median first full season was 0.25 points a game. Parekh is at 0.41. The closest picks include Mikhail Sergachev and Dougie Hamilton. He's shooting just 3.7%, so a few more goals should come, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking (a small, seven-game sample) has him as a setup man. The thing to watch now is his own end against tougher minutes. That will decide whether this is a power-play specialist or a top-pair defenseman. We project 28 points.
headline: Zayne Parekh says he belongs. He's right.
